moat_against: Economics reset at rights renewals (Concorde/FIA through 2030, broadcasters, promoters) — the fade horizon is contractual
Team payments consume roughly half of F1 revenue and the teams bargain collectively
Calendar/geopolitics risk is live: 2026 Bahrain GP rescheduled to Malaysia; Wells Fargo cut its target on Middle East risk
Post-MotoGP leverage (net debt 5.27x normalized OE; MotoGP facilities at 5.6x) thins the equity cushion
Popularity concentrated in one sport's stars and storyline; fashion/cycle sensitive
moat_for: Exclusive long-term commercial rights to F1 and MotoGP — scarce, irreplaceable global sports IP under one owner (Concorde through 2030)
Contracted escalating media-rights / sponsorship / race-promotion fees with proven pricing power (F1 revenue +14%, Adjusted OIBDA +20% in 2025)
Asset-light model: teams fund cars, drivers and R&D while Liberty collects fees — minimal capex, high incremental margins
Audience momentum (2025 attendance 6.75M, live viewership +21%) and a second property (MotoGP) for the same commercial playbook; Las Vegas GP extended through 2037
moat_justification: Liberty owns the exclusive commercial rights to the world's two premier motorsport properties — Formula 1 (Concorde Agreement through 2030) and MotoGP (acquired July 2025) — with contracted, escalating media-rights, sponsorship and race-promotion fees, proven pricing power (F1 revenue +14% and Adjusted OIBDA +20% in 2025), and an asset-light model in which teams fund the cars and R&D while Liberty collects the fees. Against that: the rights stack resets at renewals, team payments absorb roughly half of F1 revenue and teams bargain collectively, the calendar is exposed to geopolitics and host-country politics, and the post-MotoGP balance sheet is levered (net debt 5.27x normalized OE).
name: Liberty Media Corporation
one_liner: Elite scarce sports IP (F1 + MotoGP), moat 7/10 — but at $91.43 the OE yield is only 3.26% on a $2.98/share normalized base with net debt 5.27x OE, so the weighted IRR is 5.75% (IV@15% $23.45); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$23.
